title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The Transit Supplement. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. The hero photograph is fixed in every option.

options.label: The Transit Supplement
options.lineage: the folded route insert and timetable supplement issued with an intercity service
options.thesis: A trip is a service with a printed supplement. Its map shows a route with a direction of travel; its columns show when to move and where to eat. The category default stacks a photo hero over a card grid of benefits; this refuses to summarise the trip at all and instead shows the routing device the product actually produces.
options.viewport: The fixed grayscale destination photograph fills the first viewport. Below it the light paper supplement begins at full bleed with a hard seam: nested contour bands, one prussian route line drawn with a marked origin and terminus, and the three-input form set into the supplement's own ruled columns as the primary action.
options.risk: A ruled technical page can read cold if the contour work is decorative rather than load-bearing.

raised.raise: Depth and direction of travel — the route reads as movement along an axis from an origin to a terminus, never as a table row.
One fold, one silhouette — the photograph meets the paper across a single hard seam; nothing accumulates at the join.
Single-ink discipline on paper, and the trip is a dated, numbered run.
Exactly one saturated ink spent on the route line and the primary action, nothing else.
The column lattice is sacred — it scales rather than reflows, and every colour on the page means exactly one thing.

options.label: The Working Timetable
options.lineage: the ruled working timetable posted for a service
options.thesis: Constraint made legible. Every hour of the trip is accounted for in a ruled grid, because the product's real promise is that nothing on a day is wasted or double-backed.
options.viewport: Below the photograph, a full-bleed ruled time grid with the route drawn as a line threading fixed hour slots.
options.risk: The most familiar landing-page shape in this category. Named plainly: a grid of benefits is one column away from this, and it will read as a generic travel page if the time slots are not genuinely load-bearing.

options.label: Teletext Service
options.thesis: The catalogue as a broadcast index: numbered pages, not sections. Holds the audience axis — a fixed cell lattice is exactly how a planner thinks about a day.
options.viewport: A numbered page index; each day is a page address, keyed directly.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and the lattice discipline is worth keeping. Loses on product clarity: a phosphor grid says broadcast, and a trip is not broadcast.
options.risk: Reads retro-novelty the moment the grid is not strictly held.

options.label: One Ink, One Sheet
options.lineage: a hand-set newspaper printed by lamplight where a second chance does not exist
options.thesis: Everything in one ink on damp rag paper, and the compositor's errors left standing because there is no time to fix them. The single-ink discipline is the strongest of the round.
options.viewport: One dated sheet, the trip set as that day's single pulling.
options.case: Holds the audience axis through the feeling of a deadline and no second chance, which is the organiser's real scene. Loses product clarity: one ink cannot carry a route line, a budget and a primary action.
options.risk: Reads nostalgic the moment the type is set timidly.

options.label: Axial Vistas
options.lineage: the clipped geometry and forced perspective of a formal garden
options.thesis: A route read as movement along a single enforced axis, breaking only into concealed rooms.
options.case: Fuses the direction of travel beautifully but the garden's symmetry fights an itinerary, which is irregular by nature.
options.kept: Direction of travel along an axis, raised onto the assigned direction.

options.label: One Crease
options.lineage: a circular sheet raised into a shell by a single compass arc
options.thesis: One structural fold line where a flat sheet becomes rigid, drawn with a compass.
options.case: The fold is the best idea for meeting the fixed photograph and nothing else on the page earns it.
options.kept: One fold, one silhouette, raised onto the assigned direction.

options.label: Civic Bureau
options.lineage: a late-modern municipal prospectus, almost all bone-white, all colour in one ribbon
options.thesis: One continuous rendered ribbon of colour across an empty plate, and one violet button.
options.case: The single-saturation discipline is worth taking, the bone-white plate is the generic-product-page rut in another costume, and the ribbon is decoration with nothing to route.
options.kept: One saturated ink, spent only where it earns it. Raised onto the assigned direction.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What this category ships, executed impeccably: white ground, product photography, a feature grid and a single call to action.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement a visitor expects, at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
